caption: Right-click a server or database in Object Explorer and choose New Query.
Click Execute (or press F5) to run the query in the editor.
The Results grid — every profiling number in this chapter lands here.

code:
SELECT
    COUNT(*)                     AS total_rows,
    COUNT(DISTINCT CustomerID)   AS distinct_customers,
    COUNT(DISTINCT EmailAddress) AS distinct_emails
FROM Sales.Customer;
caption: If total_rows and distinct_customers don't match, you've likely found duplicates — Lesson 15's territory.

eyebrow: Profiling several columns' NULL rates at once
code:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EmailAddress IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_emails,
    SUM(CASE WHEN Phone IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)        AS null_phones,
    SUM(CASE WHEN PersonID IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)     AS null_person_id
FROM Sales.Customer;
caption: One query, three columns' NULL counts side by side — a quick first pass on any unfamiliar table.

code:
SELECT
    COUNT(*) AS total_rows,
    SUM(CASE WHEN EmailAddress IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS null_emails,
    CAST(
        100.0 * SUM(CASE WHEN EmailAddress IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END)
        / COUNT(*)
    AS DECIMAL(5,2)) AS null_email_pct
FROM Sales.Customer;
caption: 100.0, not 100 — T-SQL's integer division silently truncates a percentage to zero otherwise.
